claims.text: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has useful room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr retains useful yield strength at high temperature.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance.
A 50–100 nm alumina layer can be deposited on cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr by atomic layer deposition.
The deposited alumina layer will form a continuous film.
The deposited alumina layer will adhere to HfNbTaTiZr during exposure near 1000 °C in air.
The alumina film will act as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
The alumina coating will impede oxygen ingress into HfNbTaTiZr during high-temperature exposure.
Impeding oxygen ingress will prevent oxidation-induced microstructural degradation.
Preventing oxidation-induced microstructural degradation will preserve the alloy's mechanical properties.
Relative to uncoated cast HfNbTaTiZr, coated material will exhibit significantly reduced oxygen uptake after exposure near 1000 °C in air for up to 100 hours.
Relative to uncoated material, coated HfNbTaTiZr will maintain similar room-temperature tensile ductility after the specified exposure.
Relative to uncoated material, coated HfNbTaTiZr will maintain similar yield strength near 1000 °C at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr experiences substantial oxygen penetration under comparable high-temperature oxidizing conditions.
Oxygen penetration in untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr causes subsequent mechanical degradation.
